lesson.title: Spot the AI around you
lesson.subtitle: What AI is — and what it isn’t

video.title: Spot the AI around you
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Staff room, morning light. Close-up of Amina’s phone: she types “The exam timetable is…” in a parents’ group chat. The keyboard suggestion bar lights up with “ready”. Cut to Amina’s face: one eyebrow up, curious smile.
scenes.animation: Typing appears letter by letter; suggestion chip pops with a 150 ms bounce. Quick push-in on Amina’s face.
scenes.narration: Wait… how did my phone know I was going to type “ready”?
scenes.sound: Soft keyboard taps; light music bed starts.
scenes.vids: Phone close-up: use a flat phone illustration or record a real phone screen in the Recording studio. Character: illustrated teacher in a headscarf, ink outlines.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey card. The Darsi mark pops in, then the lesson title and a yellow ‘AI’ track chip with the spark icon.
scenes.animation: Mark scales 0→100% with a small overshoot (≤ 200 ms); title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: what AI really is — and how to spot it in things you already use.
scenes.vids: Use the Darsi title template (see brand kit). Keep the chip as icon + word.

scenes.visual: A classroom wall with a solar lamp. A clock face spins to 6:00 and the lamp switches on. A hand writes on a card: clock icon → lamp icon. Repeat once quickly to show ‘same every day’ (calendar pages flip).
scenes.animation: Clock hands spin; lamp glow appears as a flat yellow circle (no blur). Calendar flips 3 pages fast.
scenes.narration: Some machines only follow fixed steps that a person wrote. This solar lamp has a timer: at six o’clock, switch on. Every day, exactly the same. It never learns anything new.
scenes.sound: Click when the lamp switches on.
scenes.vids: Search stock illustrations for ‘solar lamp’ or draw a simple lamp shape. On-screen label sits under the scene, not on the image.

scenes.visual: Back to Amina’s phone. Behind it, hundreds of tiny message bubbles stream in from the edges and stack up (examples). A sparkle appears where the same word pairs repeat; the bubbles fade and the suggestion “ready” glows.
scenes.animation: Bubbles fly in on curved paths, 2–3 s. Sparkle pulse once. No text inside the bubbles — just lines.
scenes.narration: Your phone keyboard is different. Nobody wrote a rule that says “after timetable is, suggest ready.” Instead, it learned from a huge number of examples of how people write. It spotted a pattern — and made a best guess.
scenes.vids: Animated shapes: use the Vids shape tools or a pre-made ‘bubbles’ animation exported as a short clip.

scenes.visual: Clean definition card on white with the AI track chip. Three icons appear in a row: stack of cards (examples) → sparkle (pattern) → speech bubble with a question mark (best guess).
scenes.animation: Icons appear one by one, 300 ms apart, with arrows drawing between them.
scenes.narration: So here is our one-sentence version. Most AI today is a computer system that learns patterns from examples, then uses them to make predictions — best guesses — or decisions.
scenes.vids: Keep the card on screen for at least 6 seconds so teachers can read it in a second language.

scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: first day of term — Amina holds a seating chart and reads names. Right: weeks later at a busy market — she waves and calls a pupil by name.
scenes.animation: Wipe from left half to right half. Pupil waves back.
scenes.narration: Think of a new class. On day one you use the seating chart — a rule. A few weeks later you know every face, even at the market. You learned from examples.
scenes.vids: Market scene: stock illustration or Veo clip of a busy outdoor market (no readable signs).

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor pops in holding the solar lamp, friendly grin. Two big answer cards appear: ‘AI’ and ‘Not AI’.
scenes.animation: Character slides in from the side; answer cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! This solar lamp switches on at six every evening. Is that AI?
scenes.sound: Two gentle ‘pop’ sounds for the cards.
scenes.vids: The app pauses here (diamond marker). For the MP4 shared outside the app, hold this frame for 3 seconds with a small countdown ring.

scenes.visual: The ‘Not AI’ card gets a blue check badge. Next to it, the rule card (clock → lamp) reappears.
scenes.animation: Check badge pops (150 ms). Quick 0.8 s confetti of three shapes in kola, sunbird and ink.
scenes.on_screen_text: Not AI — it follows one rule
scenes.narration: Not AI. It follows one fixed rule a person set. Useful — but it doesn’t learn.
scenes.vids: Use blue for correct (never green) and always pair it with the check icon.

scenes.visual: Fast montage, about 7 seconds each: a teacher speaks into a phone and words appear as lines (voice typing); a message with a gift-box icon slides into a spam folder; a farmer points a phone at a cassava leaf and a warning badge appears; a phone map shows a river with an alert badge (flood forecast).
scenes.animation: Each card flips in from the right. Keep motion simple and readable on a small screen.
scenes.narration: Once you know the pattern, you’ll spot AI everywhere. Voice typing that turns your speech into text. Spam filters that move “You won a prize!” messages out of your inbox. Apps that look at a photo of a cassava leaf and warn about disease. Flood forecasts that warn communities days ahead. Each one learned from lots of examples.
scenes.vids: Use flat icons from the Darsi set on white cards. Do not show real app logos or brand names on screen.

scenes.visual: Three grey cards: a calculator, a traffic light, a school bell. Each gets a small ‘rule’ card (list icon) beside it.
scenes.animation: Cards slide in together; rule cards stamp on one after another.
scenes.narration: And some things that are usually not called AI: a calculator, a traffic light on a fixed timer, an automatic school bell. They follow fixed steps. They don’t learn.
scenes.vids: Keep these cards in neutral colours (no track colour) so ‘AI’ stays visually distinct.

scenes.visual: Three answer cards: calculator, voice typing, school bell. Amina points at the cards and looks at the viewer.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which one of these uses AI?
scenes.vids: Second diamond marker — the app pauses for the question. In the MP4, hold for 3 seconds, then highlight ‘voice typing’.

scenes.visual: ‘Voice typing’ card gets the check badge, then the screen resolves into three summary cards: rule card (person writes it), examples stack (AI learns), speech bubble with question mark (best guess).
scenes.animation: Cards line up left to right, 250 ms apart.
scenes.narration: Voice typing — yes! Remember: rules are written by people. AI learns from examples. And what AI gives you is a prediction — a best guess.
scenes.vids: Hold the three cards for 5 seconds.

scenes.visual: Amina’s classroom. The board has two chalk boxes. Pupils hold up picture cards and place them in a box; one pupil explains, others nod. End card: Darsi mark and ‘Next: How machines learn from examples’.
scenes.animation: Cards fly from pupils’ hands to the board. End card fades in.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: draw two boxes on the board — learns from examples, and follows a rule. Call out everyday things and let your pupils decide, and explain why.
scenes.sound: Music resolves; no end jingle longer than 1 s.
scenes.vids: Classroom: illustrated pupils in local school uniforms; avoid stereotyped imagery. End card from the Darsi template.

checkpoints.prompt: The solar lamp switches on at 6 pm every day. Is that AI?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it follows one fixed rule a person set. It doesn’t learn from examples.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the lamp follows a timer a person set. Nothing is learned from examples, so it isn’t AI.

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — voice typing learned from many recordings of people speaking.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — that one follows fixed rules. Voice typing is the one that learned from examples of speech.

video.vids_prompt: Create a 3 minute animated explainer video for teachers titled “Spot the AI around you”. Style: flat, friendly illustration with bold ink outlines, light grey backgrounds, a tangerine (#ff6a2b) brand colour and a sunny yellow (#ffc53d) accent; no gradients or blur. Main character: Amina, a primary school teacher. Follow the attached script scene by scene: a phone keyboard suggests the next word; a solar lamp timer that follows a rule; AI learns patterns from examples and makes a best guess; examples of AI (voice typing, spam filters, crop disease apps, flood forecasts) and non-examples (calculator, fixed traffic light, school bell); two quick quiz pauses; end with a classroom sorting activity. Use the narration exactly as written, a warm, calm voice, and keep on-screen text to six words or fewer per scene.
